text:
Elena (partnerships): Heads-up: Billing flagged ~150 accounts hitting entitlements right at midnight PST last night. Marketplace export shows `usage_date` that seems to be local-midnight-aligned, but our billing windows are UTC. Anyone seen this before?
Sam (eng): Which marketplace? Azure or Google?
Elena (partnerships): Azure. The CSV rows include `usage_date` like 2026-11-02 (no timezone). Suspect it's local-start-of-day.
Ravi (eng-infra): We've seen similar with a few SI integrations. If the partner reports day-local values, recon that buckets by calendar-day will drift across timezones.
Lina (finance): We're getting a few angry customers asking why they hit caps. Need a short-term fix and a comms plan.
Elena (partnerships): Example snippet from the export:
```
acct,usage_date,units,sku,region
ACCT-3019,2026-11-02,450,REDWOOD-PRO-1,us-west-2
ACCT-3019,2026-11-03,10,REDWOOD-PRO-1,us-west-2
```
Sam (eng): Quick mitigation: when ingestion sees a bare date, consult customer profile for timezone and convert date->UTC bucket. We don't currently store a canonical tz per customer though.
Ravi (eng-infra): We can derive a likely tz from `region` for many customers (us-west-2 -> PT). Not perfect but covers majority. I'll add a flag to enable heuristic mapping: `enable_marketplace_tz_heuristics`.
Lina (finance): For billing ops: prepare a "temporary hold" label for invoices affected and a draft credit policy if recon changes more than 2% of billed units.
MeteringBot (bot): created ticket PRT-2109: "az-marketplace-day-boundary-reconcile" priority P1.
Elena (partnerships): Action list: Sam -> patch ingestion to accept `reported_date` and attempt tz normalization (feature-flagged). Ravi -> implement heuristics + log scoring confidence. Lina -> create invoice-hold workflow and draft customer note. I'll reach out to Azure account rep asking them to include an ISO timestamp in future exports.
Sam (eng): I'll open PR `recon/az-date-to-utc` with unit tests. Plan: if customer.tz exists use that; else fallback to region->tz map; else mark low-confidence and keep as-is for manual review. Will add dry-run mode to see how counts change for last 14 days. ETA: tomorrow morning.
Ravi (eng-infra): I'll add a reconciliation audit table that records original row, adjusted_utc_day, and confidence_score. Ops can review low-confidence shifts before any billing changes.
Lina (finance): Can we run the dry-run and produce a delta file that shows per-account change percentiles? I want to route anything >1% to billing review.
Sam (eng): Yes. Dry-run will output CSV with `acct,original_day,adjusted_day,units,delta_pct,confidence`.
Elena (partnerships): Also worth asking Azure if they can include `usage_start_ts`/`usage_end_ts` in the export. That'd remove ambiguity. I'll draft that ask.
Ravi (eng-infra): For immediate relief, Ops can implement a rolling window rule: until we validate, don't auto-apply adjustments that move >10% of a day's units across buckets. We'll surface those for manual decision.
Lina (finance): Agree. I'll prepare a template credit memo and get legal eyes. Send impacted account list to billing@ for approval before issuing credits.
Elena (partnerships): Thanks all. Please paste PR links and the dry-run CSV in this thread when ready. :pray:
Sam (eng): Will do.
Ravi (eng-infra): I'll kick off heuristics feature flag behind `enable_marketplace_tz_heuristics` once PR lands.
Lina (finance): Standing by to review deltas and approve credits where appropriate.
Elena (partnerships): Closing for now; will follow up after dry-run results.
